deltas.delta: In v2.12.0-beta the memo calls uint256.MulModWithReciprocal, whose full-width branch (uint256 v1.3.2 uint256.go lines 688-715) runs the same reduce4 as MulMod (lines 720-730) with a cached reciprocal, and reduce4 writes the destination only after reading the modulus (mod.go lines 334-467). The memo is replaced whenever any limb of the modulus differs (mulmod_memo.go). A copy of the memo linked against uint256 v1.3.2 equals math/big on 3,000,000 MULMOD inputs, one quarter of them with modulus 2^256-1 and one quarter with a full-width modulus whose top 128 bits equal the high half of the product. A planted one-bit fault was caught 523 times in 200,000 cases. A stale reciprocal does not give a wrong word: it made reduce4 run without end in a planted test, so a memo fault would show as a stalled node, not a wrong price.
Polygon mainnet has PragueBlock 73,440,256 and OsakaBlock nil in bor develop and v2.11.2, so the Prague instruction set applies and CLZ does not exist there. HampiBlock is nil (unscheduled).

findings.title: 48 Club's BNB Smart Chain node answers from an unpublished geth commit built with an end-of-life Go release
findings.difference: BNB Smart Chain has no single reference build. BNB Chain's dataseed nodes run v1.8.2-4e1c8247 (F-121), and 48 Club, one of the earliest community validators and by its own account the largest MEV builder on the chain, answers at rpc-bsc.48.club with v1.8.2-132104cd-20261116 built with go1.25.5. Neither commit is public. Go 1.25 has been out of support since go1.27 shipped on 2026-08-19, and go1.25.6 to go1.25.13 each carried compiler fixes that this build does not have.
findings.mechanism: Every arithmetic the pool math depends on runs in the node's Go code: holiman/uint256 for MULMOD in FullMath.mulDiv and SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta, SDIV and SMOD in TickBitmap.compress and flipTick, SAR and SIGNEXTEND in TickMath and BalanceDelta. A miscompiled routine or a private patch in a builder or validator build would change a swap or a liquidity amount in the blocks that build produces, and the other validators would then reject those blocks, so the visible effect is a missed or reorganised block and not a wrong balance that stays. On the 48.club endpoint the build gives the specified result on all 99,985 battery vectors, all 85,544 targeted vectors, all 50 call semantics words and all 12,198 slot reads, and the same records as Ethereum's node on 250 of 250 first-set scripts and 300 of 300 second-set scripts. On the sixth set it equals the reference interpreter on 703 of 706: script 682 names system contract 0x1000 as a currency, as on every BSC endpoint, and scripts 277 and 279 stop at a swap that its 50 million gas cap cannot afford, as on Avalanche. Whether 48 Club's validators run the same commit as its RPC node is not public.
findings.impact: No loss path for any user was found. The finding records that block production on BSC may run code that no one outside the operator can read, built with a toolchain that no longer gets fixes.
findings.preconditions: A fault in the unpublished commit or a miscompile in go1.25.5 on a path the tests above do not reach, inside a validator or builder that produces blocks. Only the operator can bring this about.
findings.mitigations: Rerun the opcode battery, targeted set and script sets on rpc-bsc.48.club after each 48 Club build change and after Jenner. Ask BNB Chain and 48 Club to publish the commits their nodes run.

The operand edges that TickMath (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:61-63), FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 48, 112), SqrtPriceMath (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:219, 252) and TickBitmap (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:20-26, 38, 54-67) depend on therefore behave as specified.

cleared.result: 50 of 50 as specified everywhere. No transient slot folds. The only persistent aliases are the Avalanche bit-248 fold of F-040 and the truncation masks of a base slot whose top byte is 0x01, the same as cycle 15 and opcodes/statekeys.json.

cleared.check: pmdiff.py (250 scripts), pmdiff2.py (300 scripts) and pmdiff6.py (706 scripts) on the networks.json endpoints, and pmdiff and pmdiff2 again on QuickNode for Polygon and on 48.club for BSC.
cleared.result: Every result equals the recorded one. BSC and Avalanche: 249 or 250 of 250 and 300 of 300 identical with Ethereum (the missing one is the script Ethereum itself could not complete in that run). Polygon on both bor endpoints: the same 19 first-set and 20 second-set scripts differ as recorded in opcodes/pmdiff.json and opcodes/pmdiff2.json, all of them heavy swaps that run out of gas at 25 million, and the reference hashes equal the recorded ones. Sixth set: Polygon and BSC differ only on script 682 (currency 0x1000, a system contract there), Avalanche only on 277 and 279, as recorded in opcodes/pmdiff6.json.

cleared.check: holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 (bor, BSC) and v1.2.4 (avalanchego) executed directly, in the operand aliasing each interpreter uses, against math/big: MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, EXP, SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND and the five comparisons, plus a copy of bor v2.12.0-beta's MULMOD memo.
cleared.result: No mismatch in 3,000,000 cases per operation per version (750,000 for EXP). The inputs mix limb boundary and sign edges, the TickMath constants, modulus 2^256-1 on a quarter of the MULMOD cases and a full-width modulus sharing the top 128 bits of the product's high half on another quarter, shift and byte indices up to 259, and sign extension indices up to 39. Planted one-bit faults in the memo result and in SAR by 255 were caught 523 and 754 times in 200,000 cases. This is the first execution of the library code itself in the review; earlier cycles tested it only through the nodes and by reading.

cleared.check: Leads L-032 and L-161 on the releases after v2.11.1: does any change to BlockSTM, its serial fallback or the merge of results let transient storage pass from one transaction to the next.
cleared.result: No. The executor, state database, journal, transient storage and state transition files are byte identical in v2.11.1, v2.11.2 and v2.12.0-beta, and the parallel state processor differs only in one error message. Cycle 11's reading therefore holds for every Polygon build that is released or proposed: each incarnation starts from a fresh state copy, Prepare installs a new transient map, and transient storage is not in the multi-version write set that the merge copies. The PoolManager's lock, deltas and synced currency (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36) cannot leak across transactions on any of these builds.

cleared.check: Does 48 Club's virtual contract at 0x48, which its RPC uses to identify itself, change what a contract call to that address returns, so that a currency or recipient 0x48 behaves differently on its nodes.
cleared.result: No. Only a top-level eth_call with value 0x30 returns 0x30. A call from a contract to 0x48 with value 0 or 0x30 succeeds with empty return data on both the 48.club build and the BNB Chain build, which is how an empty account answers everywhere. A take of currency 0x48 (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75) or a native payout to it (src/types/Currency.sol:48) therefore behaves the same on every BSC node.
cleared.source: https://docs.48.club/privacy-rpc; eth_call with state override on https://rpc-bsc.48.club and https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, 2026-11-25

cleared.check: Upcoming forks angle: assume every upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships (BSC Jenner on 2026-12-08, Polygon Salvador at block 98,688,600 and bor v2.12.0 with the MULMOD memo and the widened keccak cache, Avalanche Igloo if it is scheduled). What can an ordinary account do the day after to funds already in the PoolManager?
cleared.result: Nothing new beyond recorded findings. Jenner adds no opcode and changes no core/vm handler (master equals v1.8.2), and its CAS20 and 0x70 addresses become token or time precompiles whose issuer powers are F-007 and F-076 (issuer level) and whose fork boundary was cleared in cycle 12; BEP-703 reserves part of block gas for BNB transfers, which only tightens the per-block bound of F-111 and F-115. Salvador gives code to five accounts that hold no claims or positions (F-134, governance level) and is in no release yet. bor v2.12.0's memo returns the stock MULMOD result as executed this cycle, and its keccak cache keys on full input copies (cycle 16), so FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 48), pool ids (src/types/PoolId.sol:14) and position keys (src/libraries/Position.sol:60) compute the same values. Avalanche has no scheduled upgrade, and Igloo's tracked items concern Subnet-EVM L1s.

leadResults.answer: No Polygon endpoint runs bor v2.12.x on 2026-11-25 (publicnode v2.11.1-private, QuickNode v2.11.1, OnFinality and Tatum v2.11.2; drpc, Tenderly and 1rpc hide the build). New evidence covers the memo itself: a copy of mulmod_memo.go linked against holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 equals math/big on 3,000,000 MULMOD inputs with the interpreter's aliasing, a quarter at modulus 2^256-1 and a quarter at the full-width shape of the ruint fault, and a planted fault is caught. MulModWithReciprocal runs the same reduce4 as MulMod, so the memo changes only where the reciprocal comes from. The node rerun with and without --precompile-cache is still owed.
v2.12.0 has not shipped; v2.12.0-beta is still the newest tag (23 Nov). Nothing to recheck until the release exists.

The BlockSTM executor, the serial path and the state files are byte identical in v2.11.1, v2.11.2 and v2.12.0-beta, and the parallel processor differs only in one error string. Cycle 11 read v2.11.1: each incarnation starts from a fresh copy, Prepare installs a new transient map, and transient storage is not merged. The result equals serial execution for transient storage on every released or proposed build.

The merge step copies only persistent paths of the multi-version write set (cycle 11, statedb.go lines 295-305 and 693-702 in v2.11.1), and those files are unchanged in v2.11.2 and v2.12.0-beta. Transient storage is never copied into the state a later task reads.

Answered by cycles 2 and 9 from source and rechecked against v1.15.3, which the endpoints still run: saexec applies each transaction with core.ApplyTransaction (execution.go line 351), libevm's state transition calls Prepare, which installs a new transient map, and end-of-block operations (lines 402-429) are balance and nonce writes with no EVM call. The file has moved on master, which is filed as a new low lead.

For blocks 135,480,000 to 135,489,999, rpc-bsc.48.club returns 24,459 PoolManager logs in 7,925 blocks, and its count equals the receipts of dataseed1 in all 40 sampled blocks. bsc-rpc.publicnode.com (reth-bsc) returns 0 logs and no error for the whole window, but 141 of 141 for a recent 100 block window, so it serves only recent log history and reports nothing for older blocks. bsc-dataseed1 and dataseed2 refuse eth_getLogs for any range with 'limit exceeded'. Scripts in cycles 5, 6, 7, 9, 13 and 16 name the publicnode endpoint; whether each used it for old blocks is filed as a new medium lead. This is recorded as a profile delta and not as a hazard.

Commit 4e1c8247 is still not readable and both dataseed endpoints still report it. The public tag v1.8.2-td-enhancement (4bd1c73, 17 Nov) has the same core/vm, core/state, params and go.mod as v1.8.2. A third unpublished build, 132104cd of 16 Nov with go1.25.5, now answers at rpc-bsc.48.club (new info finding). Which build validators run into Jenner is not public.

Operator level. Public builds on 2026-11-25: Polygon publicnode go1.26.10 (inside the miscompile range), QuickNode, OnFinality and Tatum go1.26.11 (fixed); BSC dataseed go1.26.10, 48.club go1.25.5 (outside the range but out of support); Avalanche go1.26.10. Validator builds are not published.

The release that activates Jenner is v1.8.2 itself, which master equals in core/vm and core/state, and the later tag 4bd1c73 is identical too. All pre-fork reruns were done on dataseed1, dataseed2, reth-bsc and the new 48.club build on 2026-11-25 with no difference from the recorded results. The rerun within a day of 2026-12-08 02:30 UTC cannot be done in this cycle and stays owed.

The C-Chain still has no delegated accounts: a 0xef0100 designator fails with invalid opcode 0xef on avalanchego 1.15.3 on 2026-11-25, while BSC and Polygon resolve it. No upgrade that could add them is scheduled; Igloo is unscheduled on Mainnet and Fuji and its tracked items concern Subnet-EVM L1s. Hazards that need a delegated account therefore do not apply on Avalanche until a scheduled upgrade says otherwise.
